skip_reason: Not a sales call. This is a same-day service-recovery call: Cameron, the branch manager, called an existing customer (Susan Rubio) after her move was cancelled mid-job following a crew-conduct blowup, opening with 'I understand that Alex kinda brief me... I was hoping to, you know, just kinda hear what your experience was.' The entire call is complaint intake, an apology, a declined damage claim, and a full charge waiver ('we're absolutely not gonna charge you for any of the labor done today'). The customer had already rebooked with another company for the next morning. No quote form recap, no pricing pitch, no clock explanation, no estimate, no booking — the sales scorecard does not apply.
top_strength: Cameron let her tell the whole story before he tried to fix anything, and when she got to the part that actually mattered he stopped and named it instead of smoothing past it: 'that's an exert thing to say... obviously it's more than a box, there's these items inside of the box that you know, you aren't aware of... there's absolutely no reason to kick a Dolly into it.' He also corrected live misinformation the crew had given her rather than defending the crew — she was told 'I'm stuck with two trucks' and 'you signed it, you got it,' and Cameron answered 'that's not how we operate — we can, if we get to a site and it turns out we don't need two trucks, we can easily send one back,' then again later, 'that absolutely does not require two trucks and you would absolutely not be required to keep those trucks on site.' He caught the detail she buried ('Did you say that you asked them not to remove the couches from the boxes and they removed them?'), offered a damage claim on the chipped antique nightstand unprompted and pushed back once when she declined ('Are you positive?'), acknowledged the grief context she raised about her mother's things with 'Of course,' waived all charges without being negotiated down to it, and closed by thanking her: 'I appreciate you taking the time to explain the situation to me.'
coaching_note: Not gradeable on the sales rubric, but the recovery had one real hole worth coaching: Cameron committed to a full waiver verbally and never nailed it down. She said plainly 'I just want a refund' and he answered 'we absolutely are not gonna charge you for any services whatsoever' — but no dollar amount, no card, no timeline, and no written confirmation. She had been quoted near $4,000 for two trucks and believed one truck was about $2,000, so 'no charges' is ambiguous between a zero invoice and a refund of money already captured. The line he needed was, 'Susan, here's exactly what I'm doing: I'm zeroing out today's job entirely, so nothing hits your card, and if anything already posted you'll see it back in three to five business days. I'm sending you an email in the next ten minutes confirming that in writing, plus my direct line.' Second gap: he promised 'I'm going to follow up with those three employees' with no visible ownership loop back to her — a one-line 'I'll call you Monday and tell you what came of it' converts a waiver into a retained customer. Escalations for Amanda outside the grading, all from the customer's account and unverified on our side: (1) alleged profanity directed at a customer — 'I don't need this fucking job, I have money' — plus a second crew member saying he didn't want to work for her, named as Blaine, Ashton, and Isaiah, with Tyler explicitly excluded as the one who behaved; (2) she volunteered 'Blaine doesn't need to be a supervisor because he can't work well with customers,' which is a supervisor-level conduct issue, not a mover issue; (3) the crew told her the two-truck contract was locked, which is straight-up false and is a sales/ops truth-in-quoting problem independent of the conduct; (4) damage to an antique nightstand and a Dolly kicked into boxes marked fragile, with the claim declined by the customer — worth logging anyway since she declined on the grounds it 'wasn't that big a deal,' not that it didn't happen; (5) she disclosed her mother's recent death and her own health problems, so any follow-up needs to be handled by a person, not an automated survey.
phone_presence_notes: Cameron absorbed roughly fifteen minutes of raw frustration without defensiveness or excuse-making, sided with the customer explicitly ('I definitely agree with you there'), and she de-escalated enough by the end to volunteer 'it's not a reflection on Einstein, it's a reflection on those guys' and close with 'I appreciate it' — held back from a 5 only by the abrupt 'So, I'm gonna cut you off' and a stretch of stacked one-word acknowledgments ('Right.' 'Correct.' 'Oh, my.') where a fuller response was available.
audio_review_reason: Cameron's side of the transcript is heavily mangled by transcription ('I run off the bit,' 'I'd love an opportunity to kind of make a me and write our wrong here,' 'they're also pretty just half password with the not be very safe with the items'), so his actual wording on the apology, the waiver commitment, and the 'I'm gonna cut you off' interruption cannot be judged from text — and because this call contains a profanity-to-customer allegation and a full charge waiver, the audio should be pulled and retained for the conduct investigation regardless of the grading.
